page: Microsoft Azure L64aos_v5 is a virtual server instance from the Laosv5 family, utilizing dedicated AMD processors built on the x86_64 architecture. Running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware accelerators.

The primary differentiator of this server configuration is its local storage capacity, which consists of 46,080 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance is also Premium Storage capable, allowing for integration with high-performance external storage volumes. In terms of CPU instruction sets, the hardware does not support advanced vector or matrix extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX, nor does it feature specialized hardware cryptography acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L64aos_v5 offers high storage and memory density per instance. This makes it a specialized option where the cost is justified by the massive local NVMe footprint rather than raw compute-to-price ratios. A key tradeoff is the lack of GPU acceleration and advanced CPU instruction sets, which limits its utility for deep learning and high-performance computing workloads.

The hardware specifications of the L64aos_v5 make it appropriate for storage-intensive and database workloads. Suitable applications include large relational databases, NoSQL databases, data warehousing, and big data analytics engines that require massive local, low-latency NVMe scratch space alongside substantial memory capacity.
